description: STM32 bare-metal Rust firmware using the Embassy async framework — #[embassy_executor::main], async GPIO blink on an LED, and an async UART echo loop. Targets the STM32F4 family (STM32F411 Nucleo/Black Pill by default; swap HAL feature + memory.x for other chips). Flash + RTT via probe-rs.

defaults.headline: Async Rust on Cortex-M with Embassy
defaults.subheadline: embassy-stm32 + embassy-executor — async GPIO + UART echo on bare-metal STM32F4.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick for STM32F/L/G series firmware in Rust when you want async/await (Embassy). For synchronous cortex-m-rt + RTIC, pick a different starter. For Raspberry Pi Pico, use rp2040-embassy.
firstSteps: Install the Cortex-M4F target: rustup target add thumbv7em-none-eabihf
Install the flasher: cargo install probe-rs --features cli --locked
Connect an ST-Link (or any CMSIS-DAP probe) to the board
Flash + RTT: cargo run --release     # runs `probe-rs run --chip STM32F411RETx` via the cargo runner
gotchas: memory.x must match the actual chip. STM32F411RE = 512K flash + 128K RAM; STM32F401RE = 512K flash + 96K RAM; STM32F103C8 = 64K flash + 20K RAM. Wrong values silently let the linker succeed then crash at boot.
embassy-stm32 requires exactly one chip feature — e.g. `stm32f411re`. Enabling two (or none) is a compile error with a misleading `time_driver_tim5 not found` message.
The cortex-m-rt link args (`-Tlink.x`, `-Tdefmt.x`) must be in .cargo/config.toml rustflags. If you put them in build.rs alone they only apply when the `build.rs` crate links, not the downstream bin.
defmt-rtt requires a running probe-rs to drain the RTT buffer. Without a probe attached at runtime the firmware will spin waiting for the RTT reader after ~1KB of logs.
Stock embassy-executor wants a time driver. `embassy-time/tick-hz-32_768` + a chip TIM peripheral is the default; forgetting to enable a time-driver feature is the #1 new-user compile error.
Changing memory.x requires `cargo clean` — cargo does not see memory.x as a build input so the linker will use a stale copy from target/.
No_std environments have no default panic handler. panic-probe (defmt-flavored) or panic-halt is MANDATORY — the build fails with `#[panic_handler] function required` otherwise.
